description: Let's boost crop yields using technology.
summary: This dashboard integrates open-access, satellite data from NASA with official Indonesian agricultural guidelines, ensuring that its recommendations are well-founded and easy to understand. With just a few clicks, users can determine which crops are suitable, the optimal time to begin planting, and how to manage crop rotation throughout the year. Moving forward, these recommendations could be further strengthened by incorporating soil moisture data, soil property information, and direct field testing.
details:
This project features a simple dashboard that provides recommendations for crop rotation. Users can either select a specific point on a map or enter its coordinates. The dashboard then retrieves data on temperature, humidity, and rainfall for that location—sourced from NASA satellites—covering the past 10 years.

This climate data is cross-referenced with the growth requirements for 28 types of food crops, secondary crops, and vegetables, based on official guidelines from the Ministry of Agriculture. Each crop is assigned a rating—ranging from "highly suitable" to "not suitable"—along with an explanation of the underlying reason, such as temperature conditions or water availability.

Based on these assessments, the dashboard generates a sequence of crops for three planting seasons per year. The crops are intentionally rotated each season to maintain soil fertility. The dashboard also includes a heatmap indicating the optimal months to begin planting each crop, as well as charts displaying both monthly and historical climate data.
projectRefs: Technical Guidelines for Land Evaluation for Agricultural Commodities (Indonesia Ministry of Agriculture, 2011)
